title: Let There Be Light
paragraphs: Before there were hills or rivers or people, there was only dark and quiet. And God spoke. "Let there be light." And light came, soft at first, the way morning creeps over a ridge. God looked at it and saw that it was good. Then God kept going: sky, sea, earth, trees, birds, creatures of every kind, and last of all, people, to share it with. The whole story begins with love making room for others. Every night since then, every dawn has been a small reminder that the dark does not get the last word. This calendar follows one thread of that light, from the very first morning all the way to a baby in a manger.
wonder: I wonder what the very first light looked like?
activity: Sit in a dark room, light one candle, and notice how much a tiny flame changes.
prayer: God of the first light, thank you for the world you made. Help us to see it and love it. Amen.
alt: A golden spark of light begins to unroll against a deep blue night, with hills and birds just appearing.
hidden: The tiny star (introduced here), plus a very small owl.
translation: Retold in our own words, with a short quotation from the King James Version.
